Package gooeygui

Class Button

java.lang.Object
gooeygui.Component
gooeygui.Button
public class Button extends Component
A clickable button that runs a method when clicked. A button can show text, an Image, or both.

The method to run is written as this::methodName, where methodName is a void method with no parameters in your class. Notice there are no parentheses after the method name.


 public class MyApp {
     private Label message;

     public MyApp() {
         Window window = new Window("My App", 400, 300);
         message = new Label("", 50, 150, 200, 30);
         window.addComponent(new Button("Say hi", 50, 100, 120, 30, this::sayHi));
         window.addComponent(message);
     }

     public void sayHi() {
         message.setText("Hi!");
     }
 }

Buttons with pictures

Give the button an Image. The picture is resized to fit inside the button without being stretched out of shape, so the image's own position and size don't matter. When a button has both text and a picture, the picture appears to the left of the text.


 Image playPicture = new Image("images/play.png");
 Button play = new Button(playPicture, 20, 20, 60, 60, this::play);

 Button save = new Button("Save", new Image("images/disk.png"), 100, 20, 120, 40, this::save);

      public Button(String text, int x, int y, int width, int height, Runnable clickAction)
      Constructs a text button with a method to run when it is clicked.
      Parameters:
      text - the text displayed on the button
      x - the x-coordinate of the top-left corner, in pixels
      y - the y-coordinate of the top-left corner, in pixels
      width - the width of the button, in pixels (at least 1)
      height - the height of the button, in pixels (at least 1)
      clickAction - the method to run when clicked, written as this::methodName
      Throws:
      GooeyGUIException - if text is null, or if width or height is less than 1

    • setText

      public void setText(String text)
      Sets the text displayed on the button. If the button shows a picture, the picture is resized to make room for the text (or to fill the button if the new text is "").
      Parameters:
      text - the new text to display, or "" for none
      Throws:
      GooeyGUIException - if text is null

    • setImage

      public void setImage(Image image)
      Shows a picture on the button, replacing any previous picture. This can be used to change a button's picture while the program runs, such as switching between "play" and "pause" pictures. 
      
 playButton.setImage(pausePicture);
      Parameters:
      image - the picture to show on the button
      Throws:
      GooeyGUIException - if image is null
